reviewer: adversarial finder (score not authoritative; see PROMPT-STANDARD "How to review a prompt")

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) — thresholds that cannot be satisfied together
gaps.problem: Items 1, 2 and 3 collide against a palette §2 forbids re-hueing. Item 2 needs ≥45 Euclidean RGB separation between all 28 rendered class pairs; item 1 allows fill alpha as low as 0.42; item 3 darkens high-density fill by 14-22%. The closest pair (commercial-high 0x1140c9 vs office-high 0x6a1cb8, raw distance 97.5) composites over mid-grey ground to 40.9 at alpha 0.42, 48.7 at 0.50, 56.5 at 0.58 — then the hatch, which darkens both members of every high-high pair, scales that by 0.78-0.86: 31.9 / 38.0 / 44.1 at hatch 0.78. Only alpha ≥ ~0.55 with the weakest hatch clears 45, and that is before AgX tone mapping compresses saturated colour further and before item 19's fog desaturation at distance. The one lever a builder would reach for is nailed shut ('may not be re-hued to widen the margin'). Two competent builders will pick different alphas inside the stated range and one of them fails item 2 through no fault of his own.
gaps.fix: Do the arithmetic in the spec and close the corner: raise item 1's alpha floor to 0.50, and state in item 2 that the 40×40 patch is measured on un-hatched fill (sample between hatch lines, or average over one full 3.0 m hatch period and divide out the stated darkening) so item 3 cannot eat item 2's margin. If both hexes must survive as-is, drop item 2's floor to 32 for the two high-density pairs and say why. Otherwise raise commercial-high toward 0x1a5ae0 or office-high toward 0x8a2ce0 in palette.js now, as a stated cross-module change with tools.md item 10 updated in the same edit, rather than discovering it in round 2.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — the highest-consequence contract in the spec is on no checklist
gaps.problem: §2 mandates lot.heading = atan2(-nx, nz) facing the road, and §7 spends a paragraph explaining that copying frontage().heading ships every building facing backwards because buildings/index.js places the front directly from lot.heading. §2 also mandates lot.y (terrain height), which buildings.spawn reads. Neither field appears in any of the 24 acceptance items. CRITIC.md is explicit that 'the acceptance checklist is the requirement set — if something is not on it and not in ARCHITECTURE, it is a suggestion, not a failure'. So the exact failure the spec warns about at greatest length is one the critic is instructed not to fail. It surfaces two waves later as a buildings bug.
gaps.fix: Add an acceptance item: 'P over world.zones.lots — for every lot, |wrapPi(lot.heading − Math.atan2(-lot.nx, lot.nz))| ≤ 0.02 rad; the point (lot.x + lot.nx*(lot.d/2 + 3), lot.z + lot.nz*(lot.d/2 + 3)) taken along the road-facing direction returns roads.isRoad !== 0; and |lot.y − terrain.getHeight(lot.x, lot.z)| ≤ 0.05 m. Also assert every lot carries nx, nz, ax, az, corner, t, y and that (nx,nz) and (ax,az) are unit and mutually perpendicular to 1e-3.'

gaps.problem: Item 17 declares api.setBrushPreview the game's only brush-cursor renderer and says tools calls it rather than drawing its own. tools.md contradicts this: line 313 allocates 'ground decal batch (footprint / zone brush …)' inside tools' own 12 draw calls, item 10 grades the zone-brush preview in tools' own zonetool_12.png, and item 15 polices preview objects in tools' ctx.group. The spec notices only half the problem — that tools.md §7 'does not yet list setBrushPreview' — when in fact tools.md positively assigns the work elsewhere. It also double-counts the draw call: §5 lists the brush preview inside zoning's typical 7, while tools.md counts it inside tools' 12. And §5 counting it as a draw call contradicts item 17's own requirement that the toggle-diff with and without a preview parked 'differs by 0'.
gaps.fix: Resolve ownership before the round starts, in one edit to both specs. Either (a) delete item 17 and §8.9 from zoning, leave the cursor with tools, and keep only zonableAt as zoning's contribution; or (b) land the tools.md change first (tools calls ctx.modules.zoning.setBrushPreview, its decal-batch allocation drops to 11, item 10 is re-pointed at zoning's renderer), and then reconcile zoning §5 — say explicitly whether the parked preview costs zoning 1 draw call (and fix item 17's 'differs by 0' to 'differs by ≤ 1') or 0.

gaps.problem: §4 states 'Two extra captures are required on top of the matrix' and 'Nothing else in this spec asks for a frame that this invocation does not produce.' Both are wrong on the spec's own text: item 1 needs an overlay-off pair at zones/12 (it says '+two screenshots'), item 3 needs an overlay-off crop at zoneswide/12, item 6(b) needs a trough frame and a peak frame, item 9 needs two frames 0.5 s apart at zoneslope/12, and item 23 needs two more 0.5 s apart at 720p. That is roughly ten additional captures at the spec's own 30-170 s each — 5 to 28 minutes the critic has not budgeted, which is precisely how an item gets silently skipped and re-litigated next round.
gaps.fix: Replace the two sentences with a short table of every capture outside the 32-frame matrix: overlay-off zones/12, overlay-off zoneswide/12, pulse-trough and pulse-peak at zones/12, the zoneslope/12 0.5 s pair, the 720p zones/12 pair, the showcase=all frame, and the two degradation URLs — each with the item it serves and the probe session it runs inside.

gaps.property: 3 (numeric) — an item with two readings and opposite verdicts
gaps.problem: Item 4 says 'mean overlay luminance in zones_22.png is 0.35–0.55 × its value in zones_12.png', measured 'on the same probePoints() crops'. In a composited frame 'overlay luminance' is undefined. Read as the crop mean, the ratio is dominated by the ground, which at 22:00 is a small fraction of noon, so the measured value lands near 0.1 and the item is unpassable no matter what the shader does. Read as the overlay-on minus overlay-off delta, it is 0.42 by construction from the mix() the same item mandates, and the item is vacuous. Builder will measure the second way and pass; critic will measure the first way and fail. Items 1-3 are meticulous about crop, size and projection; item 4 inherits none of that care.
gaps.fix: State the method: 'capture zones/12 and zones/22 each with api.setOverlayVisible(false) then (true); overlay luminance at a probe point is the mean of (on − off) over the 200×200 crop; require L22/L12 ∈ [0.35, 0.55].' Keep the frame-p99 and brightest-pixel clauses as-is — those are already well posed.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — metre thresholds graded in pixels with no scale
gaps.problem: Item 7 (front edge within 1.5 m of road-parallel, 'Evidence: zonesclose_12.png, crop over the curved street'), item 8 (0.5-2.0 m setback gap, plus 'no overlay colour falls on asphalt, kerb or sidewalk anywhere'), and item 9's closing clause (max visible gap to ground ≤ 0.3 m in zoneslope_12.png) all state a metre tolerance and then name only a PNG. Nothing gives a pixel-per-metre conversion for those cameras, and 'anywhere' is unbounded. These are the three items most likely to be contested, because the builder will eyeball them as passing and the critic will eyeball them as failing, with no shared number.
gaps.fix: Give each a probe and demote the PNG to visual record. Item 7: P over the overlay front-edge vertex ring vs roads.sample(edgeId, t) — max perpendicular deviation ≤ 1.5 m over the curved and diagonal edges, sampled every 2 m. Item 8: P over the same vertices vs the geometric frontStart — clearance ∈ [0.5, 2.0] m for every sample, and separately assert no overlay vertex lies where roads.isRoad returns 1. Item 9: P comparing each overlay vertex y to terrain.getHeight(x,z) + the declared 0.16/0.26 lift — max residual ≤ 0.3 m.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — the prescribed remedy cannot move the prescribed metric
gaps.problem: Item 12 tells the builder to extend the end lot 'up to 3 m toward the junction' and then grades 'no notch of unclaimed zoned cells larger than 2 cells within 12 m of any of those N nodes'. Lot cell membership is quantised to the 8 m grid (lot.cells is a list of cell keys), so a 3 m geometric extension claims zero additional cells and cannot change the measured quantity at all. A builder who does exactly what item 12 says still fails item 12's check. Item 11's '±8 m of corner extension allowed' also disagrees with item 12's 3 m.
gaps.fix: Restate the corner rule in the same units as its check: 'the end lot of each run claims the corner cells of its own frontage band (lot.corner === true) and may grow by one slot, so w increases by ≤ 8 m and d is unchanged' — then align item 11's tolerance to that same ≤ 8 m and keep the ≤2-cell notch probe as the check.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — an item whose subject is undefined
gaps.problem: Item 13's organic-boundary test counts direction changes: '≥ 12 over the showcase's river frontage run, ≥ 8 over the hillside run'. Nothing defines where either run starts and stops. The zoned area's ordered boundary is one closed loop containing grid-straight street edges as well as the two organic stretches; whichever sub-run the critic picks determines the count, and the builder will pick a different one. This is the same 'which pixels' problem §4 solved so carefully for items 1-3, left unsolved here.
gaps.fix: Extend the build-record requirement (which already carries probePoints and the N node ids) with the two boundary runs: 'the first and last cell key of the river-frontage boundary run and of the hillside boundary run'. The critic walks exactly those two runs.

gaps.property: 7 (dependencies and their real APIs) — an exhaustive list that omits what the showcase needs
gaps.problem: §7 says of world.terrain 'These are the only functions this module may call; nothing else exists', then lists getHeight/getNormal/getSlope/isWater/raycast/cellSize/resolution/seaLevel. It omits world.terrain.features (src/modules/terrain/index.js:58-63), which exposes river.zAt(x), river.halfWidthAt(x), coast.xAt(z) and island — installed with the comment 'generation features for other modules (bridges, coast roads, democity layout)'. §8.5 and §8.6 require the showcase to stage a waterfront run following the river and a hillside street climbing past slope > 0.42 rad, and features is the only deterministic way to find them at seed 1337. The builder must either violate §7's exhaustive clause or brute-force sample isWater/getSlope over a 2048 m map, and the spec never says which is intended.
gaps.fix: Add the features block to §7's terrain listing, copied from terrain/index.js, plus minHeight/maxHeight, and say in §8.5/§8.6 'place the waterfront run from world.terrain.features.river.zAt(x) and the hillside run by walking getSlope until it exceeds 0.42 rad; record the resulting coordinates in the build record alongside the zoneslope target.'

gaps.problem: Four smaller items are opinions in checklist clothing. Item 18: 'clearly distinguishable from painted land and from unzonable ground' — no number, while the same item numbers its alpha to two decimals. Item 19: '~600 m' and '~150 m' blocks name no crop locations, despite §4 having built probePoints precisely to stop this. Item 20's trailing 'No allocation in update() after the first frame' has no observation method (tools.md item 13 already solves this with a renderer.info.memory.geometries probe over 60 frames). Item 16's fade 'over 0.15–0.25 s' names no sampling method, and the surrounding item is otherwise the most mechanically specified in the spec.
gaps.fix: Item 18: require mean RGB distance ≥ 30 from the nearest painted class and ≥ 20 from bare ground, at named crops. Item 19: pick two probePoints (or two extra recorded coordinates) at ~150 m and ~600 m from the zoneswide camera and cite them by name. Item 20: borrow tools.md item 13's probe — geometries and JS heap flat across 60 frames after frame 1. Item 16: sample the overlay material's opacity uniform via P every 50 ms for 0.4 s after the tool:changed emit and require the 10%→90% crossing in [0.15, 0.25] s.

gaps.property: 2 (falsifiable) — cross-module event discipline is on no checklist
gaps.problem: §2 requires 'exactly one zones:changed per paint/erase/bulk call, never one per cell'; §5 and failure mode 14 require bursts coalesced to ≤1 rebuild per 60 ms; §8.11 requires one emission at the end of staging. None of these appears in §4. buildings and infoviews both subscribe to zones:changed, and failure mode 14 describes a 45 ms job becoming a 2 s stall — yet under CRITIC.md's rule the whole area is a suggestion.
gaps.fix: Add an acceptance item: 'P installs a zones:changed counter, then runs one bulk() of 20 strokes (expect exactly 1 emission), 5 separate paint() calls (expect exactly 5), and a scripted 10-edge road addition inside 200 ms (expect ≤ 4 band rebuilds from the ctx.log rebuild lines). Payload shape matches {cells:[key], lots:{added:[id], removed:[id]}} and world.zones.version increments once per emission.'

gaps.property: Rules for role prompts — content duplicated from BUILDER.md/CRITIC.md that will drift
gaps.problem: §7's closing 'Never: touch another module's group; add a light; set toneMapping, toneMappingExposure or scene.fog; call renderer.render' restates BUILDER.md's 'Stay in your lane' and ARCHITECTURE §4 almost word for word. Item 21's 'grep -rn "Math.random" src/modules/zoning/ is empty' restates both BUILDER.md's determinism rule and CRITIC.md's explicit grep instruction. Item 24 and item 20's status/error clauses restate BUILDER.md's definition of done. Low damage today, but the standard's own rule is that a change to how all builders work must be one edit to BUILDER.md, not sixteen module edits — and these three copies are the ones that would be missed.
gaps.fix: Cut the generic half of §7's Never list, keeping only the zoning-specific clauses that are genuinely module-scoped: 'never call into buildings, props, tools or simulation; world.zones writes are yours alone; lot.buildingId is written by buildings and must be preserved, never invented.' Drop the Math.random clause from item 21, keeping the seed=1337 determinism and serialize/deserialize halves, and let CRITIC.md's standing grep cover it.

gaps.problem: Item 17 grades colour match as 'ΔE ≤ 8' without naming a formula, while item 2 is explicit about 'Euclidean RGB distance' — CIE76, CIE94 and CIEDE2000 differ by roughly a factor of two on saturated hues, so builder and critic can both be right. Item 10 contains a stray backtick ('**`cells` ≥ 1500`**') that breaks rendering mid-threshold. Item 5's clamp is specified 'across the 110-660 m camera range' but items 8 and 9 grade at the core street preset, whose distance is 60 m (camera.js:26), leaving the clamp undefined at the two closest cameras it is graded in. §3's reading of cs2_1 claims 'the grass around it is still legible through the violet' — in the actual image the violet area is almost entirely building facade, so the ground-through-overlay requirement is an extrapolation from the anchor, not a reading of it.
gaps.fix: Say 'ΔE76 in CIELAB' in item 17 (and push the same wording into tools.md item 10 in the same edit). Fix the backtick. Extend item 5's range to '60-660 m' and name street_12.png/closeup_12.png as the near end. In §3, say plainly that the ground-legibility requirement extrapolates cs2_1's treatment onto ground cells, and point at the strip of tinted ground at the bottom-left of the violet block as the part of the frame that shows it.

strengths: §2's world.zones block is a verbatim copy of ARCHITECTURE §3 — no paraphrase drift — and the added fields (cellAt/lotAt/zonableAt/maxDepth) match what grid.js already installs at lines 464-466, including zonableAt's exact {edgeId,side,depth,lat,t,ix,iz} shape at line 151

§7's dependency APIs are real and verified: frontage()'s three traps (outward heading, half-width, the length−trimA−trimB<12 empty condition) are exactly what network.js:238-260 does, and the isRoad 0|1|2 vs §3-line-99 drift is correctly recorded as a core request rather than 'corrected' into the module

§6's failure modes are sourced from this project's actual critic reports, not generic advice — terrain_r1's self-lit night tufts at 6.0, effects_r1 at 6.0, environment_r1's horizon seam (issue 6, major), environment_r2's interpolated-varying hash (issue 2), roads_r1's sunk carriageway (issue 1) — every citation checks out

probePoints() as a builder/critic rendezvous for items 1-3, with the eight coordinates written into the build record and constrained to flat inland ground ≥24 m from exclusions, removes a whole class of 'which pixels did you sample' argument before it happens

The §4 evidence set is stated once, matches gauntlet.mjs's real --cameras/--times flags and output naming exactly, and openly declares and justifies its override of CRITIC.md's default 12,22 matrix instead of silently conflicting with it

Item 22's two degradation URLs are verified reachable: parseParams parses modules=, main.js:78 uses it in place of selectModules, and the expected core defaults (addEdge → -1, frontage → [], getHeight → 0) are exactly what src/core/world.js returns

Budget is consistent with ARCHITECTURE §9 and constants.js (perModuleDrawCalls.zoning = 10; 15+20+80 = 115 for the other three; the 1.0 ms cap is tighter than §9's 2 ms and says so), and it separates 'attributable to zoning' from 'scene total' with a different measurement method for each

Numbers deliberately left to staging (N corner junctions, zoneslope target, achieved cells/lots, the eight probe points) are routed into docs/builds/zoning_r<round>.json rather than invented — the right answer to 'the spec cannot know this yet'

Item 9's split of stipple (spatial, still-readable) from flicker (temporal, two-capture diff) and item 6's two alternative amplitude measurements show the author actually tried to grade each item before writing it

Lot dimensions in item 11 are consistent with the LOT_SLOTS/LOT_DEPTH constants already in palette.js, and §8.8's 1700-cell staging floor is explicitly justified as sitting above item 10's 1500 floor rather than level with it
verdict: All ten properties are present and the research behind this spec is real, not decorative: §2's world-data block is a verbatim copy of ARCHITECTURE §3 (checked character by character), the §7 dependency APIs match the code including the three frontage() traps at network.js:238-260 (heading = atan2(nx*sgn, -nz*sgn), width = e.width/2, empty when to-from < 8 — all three confirmed exactly), the isRoad 0|1|2 drift against §3 line 99 is real and correctly recorded rather than carried, the §6 failure modes cite critic issues that exist verbatim (terrain_r1 "Night tufts are self-lit" at 6.0, environment_r1 issue 6 horizon seam, environment_r2 issue 2's interpolated-varying hash, roads_r1 issue 1), the §4 gauntlet invocation matches gauntlet.mjs's real flags and its `<camera>_<time with . → p>.png` naming, item 22's degradation defaults match src/core/world.js (addEdge → -1, frontage → [], getHeight → 0), and the cs2_1 / cs2_7 / cs2_4 anchors say what the images actually show. The probePoints() device — forcing builder and critic to sample the same eight projected pixels — is the single best idea in the docs/prompts tree and pre-empts a guaranteed round-costing argument. But the spec fails its own bar in three round-costing ways. (1) Items 1, 2 and 3 are jointly close to infeasible against a palette the spec explicitly forbids re-hueing: the closest pair (commercial-high 0x1140c9 vs office-high 0x6a1cb8, raw distance 97.5) composites to 40.9 at the allowed alpha floor of 0.42 and drops to 31.9 once item 3's hatch darkens both by 22%, against item 2's floor of 45 — only alpha ≥ ~0.55 with the weakest hatch clears it, before AgX compresses saturated colour further. (2) lot.heading and lot.y — the two fields buildings.spawn consumes, and the ones §7 spends a whole paragraph warning about — appear on no acceptance item, so under CRITIC.md's "the checklist is the requirement set" a builder can ship every building facing backwards and pass. (3) Item 17 unilaterally claims the brush cursor that tools.md line 313 already allocates to tools' own 12 draw calls. Add ~6 items whose thresholds are stated in metres or ratios but graded only "in a PNG" with no scale and no probe, and roughly seven of 24 items are arguments waiting to happen. Fix the numbered gaps below and this is a 9; as written it will burn a round discovering the palette corner and a second one arguing about item 4.
